title: The Siege of Vienna
description: September-October 1529. Suleiman the Magnificent's army arrives before Vienna's medieval walls. The player commands the garrison of German Landsknechts and Spanish arquebusiers under Niklas Graf Salm: countermine the Ottoman sappers, repel assaults on the Carinthian Gate, and hold until autumn rains and supply failure force the Ottoman withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: Player Two's sole placed unit is the hero SALADIN, a Kurdish-Ayyubid sultan who died in 1193 — 336 years before 1529 and from the wrong dynasty entirely; the engine offers no Suleiman hero but does offer generic Turkish gunpowder troops and at minimum a non-named commander, so a named 12th-century hero was avoidable.

The garrison is armed with MAN_AT_ARMS and CROSSBOWMAN, i.e. 13th-14th century melee infantry and crossbows, while the brief promises Landsknechts and Spanish arquebusiers — AoE2 provides both the LANDSKNECHT and the HAND_CANNONEER, so this mismatch is avoidable.
A generic KING unit stands in for Niklas Graf Salm, a professional soldier and not a monarch; no Habsburg/Imperial commander figure is otherwise represented.

No Ottoman material culture is placed at all — no Janissaries (available in the engine), no bombard cannon or siege camp, no Ottoman-side buildings; the besieging army exists only as trigger spawns of unspecified type.

GUARD_TOWER x8 and a CASTLE represent Vienna's defences, but Vienna in 1529 was notoriously defended by an outdated single medieval curtain wall hastily earth-backed — the fortified castle-and-towers layout overstates the defences.
3083 oak trees blanket a 144x144 map for a scenario set in a densely built walled city surrounded by cleared glacis and suburbs the defenders had burned down before the siege.
